W: The supplier's quote expires Friday, but our department head will not sign the purchase request until Monday.
M: Ask the supplier to extend the price through next Wednesday.
W: I will, and I will also confirm whether the freight charge is still included.
M: Good. If both terms stay the same, we can submit the request first thing Monday.

questions.question_text: Why does the supplier's quote need to be extended?

options.text: The supplier has increased the freight charge.
The order quantity has been changed.
The department head requested a different supplier.
Internal approval comes after the quote expires.

questions.question_text: What additional term will the woman check?

options.text: Whether freight is still included
Whether the order qualifies for a bulk discount
Whether the delivery address has changed
Whether payment can be made in installments

questions.question_text: What will the woman ask the supplier to do?

options.text: Remove the freight charge from the invoice
Extend the quoted price through Wednesday
Deliver the order before Friday
Submit a new purchase request on Monday

options.text: To help Facilities activate access sooner

To register the man for orientation
To verify the man's lobby entry time

M: Customs is holding the sample shipment because the commercial invoice lists six units while the packing list shows eight.
W: Two promotional samples were added after the invoice was prepared.
M: Can you issue a corrected invoice this morning?
W: Yes. I will add the samples at zero value and send the revision to the broker.

questions.question_text: Why is Customs holding the shipment?

options.text: The invoice and packing list disagree on quantity.
The broker has not received the packing list.
The invoice lists an incorrect delivery address.
The samples were sent to the wrong port.

questions.question_text: What caused the difference in the documents?

options.text: Two samples were added later.
The packing list counted two boxes twice.
The broker removed two items.
Two items were damaged in transit.

questions.question_text: How will the woman correct the invoice?

options.text: Replace the invoice with the packing list.
Charge the samples at full retail price.
List the extra samples at zero value.
Remove the original six units.

W: A customer received a text asking her to confirm a transfer, but our system shows no transfer request.
M: Do not use the phone number in the message. Call the number already on her profile.
W: Should I freeze online transfers too?
M: Only if she says she clicked the link or shared credentials.

questions.question_text: What concern has prompted this conversation?

options.text: A legitimate transfer sent to the wrong account
A scheduled interruption to online banking
A customer unable to update her profile
A suspicious transfer-confirmation text

questions.question_text: Which number should the woman call?

options.text: The number in the text message
The number in the customer's profile
The customer's newly supplied number
The number of the receiving bank

questions.question_text: Under what circumstances may transfers be frozen?

options.text: If the customer receives any text message
If the customer clicked the link or shared credentials
If the customer confirms a legitimate pending transfer
If the profile phone number is unchanged

options.text: Tomorrow evening
Today at noon
Tomorrow at noon
On the morning of lunch service

questions.question_text: What will the woman check before suggesting 150 meals?

options.text: Whether the caterer has sufficient capacity
Whether all 146 guests have paid
Whether lunch can start later
Whether the venue can add thirty seats

options.text: Call the patient to cancel the imaging procedure.
Request a correction to the authorized location.
Reschedule the patient at the downtown clinic.
Submit a new clinical review request.
